1353.1: There is one God, Ik Oankar, the One who pervades all and is ever the same; his Name is Sat (the One who truly is); he is the Creator, the Being who dwells in all, without fear, without enmity, his form beyond time, unborn, self-existent, realised by the Guru's grace. Salok Sahaskriti, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). (The pandit) reads the books, says the sandhya prayers, and disputes; he worships stone (idols), and sits in trance like a heron; lies are on his lips, (decked out) like fine ornaments; three times a day he ponders the three-footed (Gayatri); a rosary round his neck, a tilak on his brow; two dhotis, and a cloth over his head. One who knows the work of (worshipping) God (sees that) all these rites are surely hollow. Says Nanak, one should meditate (on God) with firm faith, (but) without the True Guru one does not find the way. ॥1॥
These saloks are in Sahaskriti, a Sanskrit-coloured idiom (ਤਸੵ, of him; ਕਰੋਤਿ, does; ਸਿਮਰੰਤਿ, they remember).

Sandhya: the Brahmin's prayers and rites at dawn, noon and dusk; the three-footed one (traipal) is the Gayatri, the Rig Veda verse in three parts recited at them. The heron stands still in the water as if in trance, but is watching for fish.
1353.2: Fruitless is the birth of that one, so long as he does not know Brahm (God). By the Guru's grace many cross over the ocean of the world. (God) is the Cause of creation, all-powerful: says Nanak, after reflection, the cause (of all) is in the power of the Creator, who has established his power (in all creation). ॥2॥
1353.3: The way of the yogi is knowledge; the way of the Brahmins is the Veda; the way of the Khatri is valour; the way of the Shudra is the service of others; the way of all is (the remembrance of) the One; if anyone knows this secret, Nanak is his servant; he himself is (the image of) Niranjan, the Lord. ॥3॥
Sabadam here is the way, the duty (dharma), laid down for each.
1353.4: The one Krishna (the Lord) is the soul of all the gods, and the soul too of the gods of the gods; (in all) is the soul of Sri Vasudev (the Lord); if anyone knows this secret, Nanak is his servant; he himself is (the image of) Niranjan, the Lord. ॥4॥
Krishna here is a name of the one God.
1353.5: Salok Sahaskriti, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). There is one God, Ik Oankar, the One who pervades all and is ever the same; his Name is Sat (the One who truly is); he is the Creator, the Being who dwells in all, without fear, without enmity, his form beyond time, unborn, self-existent, realised by the Guru's grace. Where (in the end) are mother and father, where the joys of wife and sons? Where are brother, friend, well-wisher and kin, and where the attachment to family? Where is the fickle beauty of the enchantress (Maya)? Even before one's eyes she forsakes him. Only the remembrance of the Lord stays with one; O Nanak, it is obtained from the sons of the Unshakeable One (the Sants). ॥1॥
1354.1: Cursed is attachment to mother and father; cursed is attachment to brothers and kin; cursed is attachment to the delights of wife and sons; cursed is attachment to the goods of the household. Love for the Saadh Sangat (the company of the holy) alone is true and lasting; O Nanak, (those who keep it) dwell in peace. ॥2॥
1354.2: The body is perishable, its strength wanes; old age advances, and with it love for Maya; hopes grow beyond measure, (yet one is here) like a guest in the house; fearsome Dharam Raj (the judge of souls) is counting (his) breaths. The human body, so hard to obtain, falls into the well of attachment; O Nanak, his alone is the refuge: the grace of Gobind (the Lord of the universe), Gobind, Gobind, Gopal (the Lord who sustains all), (alone saves). ॥3॥
1354.3: (The body) is a fort of unbaked clay, fashioned of water (seed), plastered with blood and skin; it has nine doors, but no panels to them; it is propped up by the pillar of air (the breath). The ignorant do not remember the Name of Gobind, and think (this body) will last forever. O Nanak, in the refuge of the Saadh (the holy one), they save this body so hard to obtain, who repeat Har Har Har Har Har Hare. ॥4॥
1354.4: You shine forth, O Unshakeable One, knower of virtues, all-pervading, abundant in mercy; profound, lofty, all-knowing, boundless; you are dear to your servants; your feet are (their) resting place. O Master of the masterless, Nanak is in your refuge. ॥5॥
1354.5: Seeing a doe, the hunter takes aim and strikes with his weapons; but behold, O Nanak: one whom Gopal protects has not a single hair pierced. ॥6॥
1354.6: One may strive in many ways and do mighty deeds, with warriors serving him on all four sides; he may live in some lofty, hard-to-reach place and never call death to mind; (yet) when the command of the Lord, the Primal Being, comes, O Nanak, an ant draws out (his) breath. ॥7॥
1354.7: Love for the Shabad, a heart set on kindness, the praise (of God): one who does these deeds in Kalyug, the doubt and attachment lodged there (within him) are erased; (to him) the Lord (is seen) pervading every place. (O God,) your glance and your sight never fail to bear fruit; you dwell on the tongue of the Saadhs. Says Nanak: O Lord, Har Har Har Hare, dear (to them) is the repeating of your Name. ॥8॥
1354.8: Beauty perishes, the continents perish, the sun, the moon, the stars and the sky perish; the earth, the high-peaked mountains and the trees perish; wife, sons, brothers and dear ones perish; gold, gems and (all) the forms of Maya perish. Only Gopal, the Unshakeable One, does not perish; O Nanak, (his) Saadhs (too) are lasting. ॥9॥
1354.9: No delay in doing right, delay in doing wrong; fixing the Name firmly (in the heart), giving up greed; destroying sins in the refuge of the Sants: these marks of dharma are gained by the one, O Nanak, with whom Madhav (the Lord) is well pleased. ॥10॥
1354.10: One of shallow understanding stays absorbed in love of what perishes, in the play and the pleasures of a wife; youth, strength, golden earrings, many-coloured mansions, fine clothes: thus does Maya hold sway over him. O Unshakeable One, refuge of the Sants, O Lord, Nanak bows to you. ॥11॥
1354.11: Where there is birth, there is death; where joy, sorrow; where indulgence, disease; where high, low; where small, great; where rule, pride; where arrogance, humiliation. On the path of worldly life, destruction holds sway. The worship of Gobind in the company of the Saadh alone is lasting; O Nanak, the worship of the Lord is the food (of the soul). ॥12॥
1355.1: Where the Lord shows grace, the understanding gains the knowledge of what is real; (such) wise ones blossom, (their understanding) becomes the home of happiness; giving up pride, they keep their senses under control; their hearts are cooled, and the wisdom of the Sants is fixed firm (within them). absorbed in the sight of the Lord, they are freed from (further) birth; O Nanak, the vina of the Shabad resounds (within them). ॥13॥
1355.2: The Vedas speak, the learned ponder, the students listen, in many ways and of many kinds; (but those to whom) the Lord, Har Har, is merciful fix the highest learning (of the Name) firmly within. O Nanak, they beg the gift of the Name from the Giver, Gopal, the Guru. ॥14॥
1355.3: No anxiety (is needed) for mother, father or brothers, no anxiety at all for other people; no anxiety for wife, sons and friends, ties formed by involvement in Maya. The one merciful Lord, the Primal Being, O Nanak, is the sustainer of all beings. ॥15॥
1355.4: Wealth does not last, thoughts (of it) do not last, hopes of many kinds do not last; for love of what does not last, bound by ego, one wanders after Maya, (doing) foul and sinful deeds. The one of soiled understanding, who does not remember (God), wanders through many births and the fire of the womb. Says Nanak: O Gobind, show mercy, (grant) the company of the Saadh, the saviour of the fallen. ॥16॥
1355.5: Falling from a mountain into the nether world, burning in blazing fire, being swept away on the waves of fathomless waters: against the pain of household cares, of birth and death, many such practices do not succeed; O Nanak, the support, the support, the support is the Shabad of the Saadhs, the good. ॥17॥
1355.6: Terrible suffering, many killings, the poverty of births, great strife: all are erased by remembering the Name of the Lord, O Nanak, as fire turns wood to ashes. ॥18॥
1355.7: Remembering (God), darkness turns to light; dwelling on (his) virtues, sins are destroyed; when (he) dwells in the heart, Death's messengers are struck with fear, and one does deeds supremely pure; the listener (to his praise) is freed from birth and death; his sight, never in vain, (brings) every comfort. That Lord, mighty to give refuge, beloved of the Sants, O Nanak, brings well-being. ॥19॥
1355.8: (God) makes those left behind into leaders, and fulfils the hope of the hopeless; (by his grace) the poor become rich; he cuts away the diseases of the sick; to his devotees he gives the gift of devotion, of the Name of Ram and of the singing of his virtues. The Supreme Lord, the Primal Being, is the Giver; O Nanak, what is not found through serving the Guru? ॥20॥
1355.9: The Name of Narhar is the support of the unsupported, the wealth of the poor; Gobind is the master of the masterless, Keshav the strength of the weak; the Unshakeable One is merciful to all beings, Damodar the kinsman of the lowly; the all-knowing Lord, the Being who pervades all, loves devotion and is compassion itself; Vasudev, the Supreme Lord, the Supreme God, dwells in every heart. Nanak begs this grace of the Merciful One: may Narayan never be forgotten, never be forgotten. ॥21॥
Narhar, Keshav, Damodar, Vasudev and Narayan are names of Vishnu; in Gurbani they are names of the one God.
1356.1: I have no strength, I am no servant, I have no love (for you), O Supreme Being, highest of beings; by your grace alone, O merciful Lord, Har Har, the Guru, Nanak remembers (your) Name. ॥22॥
1356.2: (God) nourishes and sustains (all) beings, and gives the gifts of shelter and clothing; the wise and conscious (Lord) creates the jewel of (human) birth. By his grace (beings) live in comfort and bliss; those who remember the Lord, Har Har Hare, O Nanak, stay free of attachment to the passing creation. ॥23॥
1356.3: Through gifts given in former lives, kings enjoy (their realms); but those whose understanding turns perverse in this mortal world, O Nanak, suffer pain for a long time. ॥24॥
1356.4: Those who are bereft of Gobind's grace, in whose hearts is no remembrance of him, even when healthy are gravely ill, for they have forgotten the Compassionate One. ॥25॥
1356.5: To dwell only on the praise (of God) is the highest dharma of those who bear a body. O Nanak, drinking the Amrit Name of Narayan, the Sants are never sated. ॥26॥
1356.6: The Sants are forbearing by nature; to them friend and evil-doer are alike; O Nanak, (friends) come to them with food of many kinds, and slanderers come at them with weapons. ॥27॥
1356.7: They are never scorned, never dishonoured; they are never without glory, and the sorrows of the world do not touch them, who, joining the company of the Saadh, repeat the Name of Gobind; O Nanak, those mortals dwell in peace. ॥28॥
1356.8: The Saadhs together are an army of unconquerable warriors; humility is the armour on their bodies; their weapons are the singing of Gobind's virtues; the shelter of the Guru's Shabad is the shield they hold; knowing the way to God is the horses, chariots and elephants they ride; they move without fear among the enemy's army, and charge (it) with the praise of Gopal; they conquer the whole world, O Nanak, and bring the five thieves (lust, anger, greed, attachment and pride) under control. ॥29॥
1356.9: The one of evil understanding takes to heart a mirage (the deer's thirst), a city seen in the clouds (gandharv nagar), the shade of a tree; just so false is attachment to family; O Nanak, (the Sants) remember the Name, Ram Ram. ॥30॥
1356.10: I am no treasury of the learning of the Vedas, no judge of virtues, nor have I the singing of the Name; no jewel of melody is in my throat, nor am I quick, clever and shrewd; Maya is gained by destiny and effort; (but) O Nanak, in the Saadh Sangat the fool (becomes) a pandit. ॥31॥
1356.11: One whose beautiful necklace is (the repeating of) Ram Ram, whose rosary-bag (hasat uch) is the love held (in the heart), who utters with the tongue the sublime verses (of praise): he is saved from (Maya), the delight of the eyes. ॥32॥
Hasat uch (the raised hand) is the gomukhi, the cloth bag in which the hand tells the rosary, held up at the chest.
1356.12: The mortal who is without the Guru's mantra: cursed is the life of that corrupt one; that fool is the equal of a dog, a pig, a donkey, a crow, a snake. ॥33॥
1356.13: One who worships the lotus feet (of God) and holds the Name in the heart, and sings the praise (of God) in the Saadh Sangat: O Nanak, Death's messengers do not even look at him. ॥34॥
1357.1: Wealth and beauty are not hard to obtain, nor is the kingdom of heaven hard to obtain; fine foods and relishes are not hard to obtain, nor are clean clothes hard to obtain; sons, friends, brothers and kin are not hard to obtain, nor are the pleasures of a wife hard to obtain; skill in learning is not hard to obtain, nor is it hard to be clever and quick; hard to obtain is the Name of the one Lord alone; O Nanak, it is found in the Saadh Sangat, by God's grace. ॥35॥
1357.2: Wherever one looks, there (God) is seen: in heaven, on earth, in the nether world; Gobind pervades all places; O Nanak, no stain, no blemish touches (him). ॥36॥
1357.3: Poison becomes Amrit, enemies become friends and one's own people; pain becomes comfort, and the one gripped by fear becomes fearless; the homeless find a resting place in the Name, O Nanak, (when) the Lord, Har Har, the Guru, is merciful. ॥37॥
1357.4: The giver of a gentle nature to all gives it to me; the purifier of all is my purifier; the maker of all is my maker; O Nanak, no stain, no blemish touches (him). ॥38॥
1357.5: The moon god is not (so) cooling, nor is the fragrant white sandal (bawan chandan); nor is the winter season (so) cooling; O Nanak, it is the Saadhs, the good, who bring coolness. ॥39॥
1357.6: The Name, Ram Ram, for one's mantra; meditating on (God) as filling all places; understanding pain and pleasure as alike; a way of life pure and free of enmity; kindness to all beings everywhere; keeping clear of the five faults; the praise of Gopal for one's food; remaining untouched by Maya, as the lotus in the water; the teaching to hold friend and foe alike; loving devotion to the Lord; not listening with the ears to the slander of others; giving up self-conceit and (becoming) the dust of all: the perfect beings have these six marks; O Nanak, they are named the Saadhs, the good. ॥40॥
1357.7: A goat may feed on roots and tubers, but it lives near a lion: such is the state of the world; O Nanak, sorrow and joy (alike) keep it in their grip. ॥41॥
1357.8: Deceit, faults, countless obstacles, offences, sins and filth, doubt, attachment, honour and dishonour, and pride: (those over whom) Maya (thus) holds sway wander through death and birth and hells; many remedies (tried) do not succeed. Pure (become those who) in the company of the Saadh, O Nanak, repeat the Name of Gopal, and dwell on the virtues of Gobind day after day. ॥42॥
1357.9: The refuge of the Master is a boat (to carry across); the Supreme God delights in play; the Cause of creation, the all-powerful, the perfect God, gives gifts; he fulfils the hope of the hopeless; he is the home of all good things. O Nanak, all remember the treasure of virtues; all beg (of him) as beggars. ॥43॥
1357.10: Places hard to reach become easy; great sufferings all turn to comfort; faithless slanderers who in their wandering pierced (others) with harsh words become good people; sorrow settles into joy, and the one wasted by fears becomes fearless; the fearful forest becomes a great city to dwell in: these marks of dharma (come) by God's grace: dwelling on Ram Ram in the company of the Saadh, and refuge, O Nanak, at the feet of the merciful Lord, Har Har. ॥44॥
1358.1: O (attachment), you are the unconquered warrior of the battle, mighty beyond measure, the crusher of many; ganas, gandharvas, gods, humans, beasts and birds: (all) you bewitch. Nanak bows to the Lord, the Creator, (and takes) the refuge of the Lord of the world. ॥45॥
Saloks 45 to 49 address in turn attachment, lust, anger, greed and pride, the five enemies. Ganas are the attendants of the gods, gandharvas the singers of the heavens.
1358.2: O lust, you give a dwelling in hell, and make (beings) wander through many births; you steal the mind, your reach is in all three worlds, you tear apart prayer, austerity and good conduct; fickle one, you give little pleasure and leave (beings) bereft (of the wealth of virtue); you pervade the high and the low. In the company of the Saadh one is freed from fear of you; Nanak (has taken) the shelter of Narayan. ॥46॥
1358.3: O anger, root of strife, compassion never springs up (in you); you bring sensual beings under your sway, and make them dance like a monkey; Death's messengers punish with many decrees the men made base in your company. The merciful God, destroyer of the pains of the lowly, O Nanak, protects all beings. ॥47॥
1358.4: O greed, even the foremost are sunk in your company, and frolic on your countless waves; beings (in your grip) run about in many ways, and waver in many fashions; because of you, they have no shame before friend, nor revered one, nor kin, nor mother and father; (in your power, one) openly does what should not be done, eats what should not be eaten, contrives what should not be contrived. Nanak's prayer to the Lord, Narhar: save me, save me, O Master, (I am in your) refuge. ॥48॥
1358.5: O pride, root of birth and death, sinful of soul, (under you) beings forsake friends and hold fast to enemies, spreading out Maya's many sprawls; coming and going, beings grow weary, and suffer much pain and pleasure; in doubt they wander in a fearsome wilderness, (caught in) dreadful, incurable diseases. The physician is the Supreme Lord, the Supreme God; O Nanak, worship (him), Har Har Hare. ॥49॥
1358.6: O Gobind, Master of the breath of life, store of mercy, Guru of the world; O remover of the world's fever, embodiment of compassion, take away all suffering; O mighty to give refuge, home of mercy, Master of the meek, show grace, (that) in the body's health and in its decline Nanak may remember (you), O Ram, Damodar, Madhav. ॥50॥
1358.7: The refuge of the lotus feet (of God), the uttering of Gopal's praise, (through these,) in the company of the Saadh, O Nanak, one crosses the great ocean, so fearful and so hard to cross. ॥51॥
1358.8: The Supreme Lord guards the head and brow, the Supreme God guards the hands and body; Gopal, the Master, guards the soul, the Lord of the world guards wealth and feet; the merciful Guru (God) guards all, and destroys fear and pain. Lover of devotion, Master of the masterless: Nanak (has come to) the refuge of the Unshakeable Being. ॥52॥
1358.9: He whose power holds up the sky, and keeps fire wrapped within wood; whose power has set light in moon, sun and stars, and breath in bodies; whose power sustains (beings) in the mother's womb, (so that) the affliction of the womb does not destroy them; by that power he props up the lake (of the world); O Nanak, the waves of its water do not destroy (its beings). ॥53॥
1359.1: The Master of the world is supreme in being; remembering him is the life of all. Through the company of the Sants, O Nanak, is found the pure path of devotion to the Lord. ॥54॥
1359.2: The mosquito shatters the mountain, the ant crosses the mire, the cripple crosses the ocean, the darkness of the blind turns to light, (when beings) remember Gobind through the company of the Saadh; Nanak (has come to) the refuge of the Lord, Har Har Hare. ॥55॥
1359.3: As a Brahmin without the tilak, as a king without command, as a warrior without weapons: so, O Nanak, is a devotee (Vaishnav) without dharma. ॥56॥
1359.4: (God holds) no conch, no discus, no mace, nor is he dark of hue; his form is wondrous, he is beyond birth; the Vedas say (of him): neti neti (not this, not this); lofty, great, boundless is Gobind. The Unshakeable One dwells in the hearts of the Saadhs; O Nanak, the fortunate understand (this). ॥57॥
The conch, the discus and the mace are the emblems of Vishnu, and the dark hue is Krishna's.
1359.5: One's dwelling is the wilderness of the world, where one's kin are dogs, jackals and donkeys; the mind (is in) a perilous place, (drunk on) the wine of attachment, (beset by) the five thieves, mighty and untamed; (there is) wandering in fondness, attachment, fear and doubt, and the noose of ego, sharp and hard; the fire (of craving) and the water (of the senses) are untameable and dreadful; the shore is beyond reach and cannot be crossed to. O Nanak, worship Gopal in the Saadh Sangat; in the refuge of the Lord's feet, by his grace, is deliverance. ॥58॥
1359.6: When Gobind, Gopal, shows mercy, he cuts away all diseases; in the company of the Saadh, O Nanak, one dwells on (his) virtues, (abiding) in the refuge of the perfect Supreme God. ॥59॥
1359.7: A man may be handsome and sweet of speech, but in the soil of his heart is enmity; (then his) bowing is false; the Sants, the good, stay alert (to it). ॥60॥
1359.8: The heedless fool does not know that (his) breaths grow fewer day by day; the most beautiful body wastes away, devoured by the daughter of Death (old age); the man stays absorbed in the play of family, in hopes of Maya's passing pleasures; wandering and wandering through many births, (the soul) is worn out; Nanak (has come to) the refuge of the Compassionate One. ॥61॥
1359.9: O tongue, O lover of tastes, sweet things are dear to you; to the True (Name) you are dead, (and you raise) great disputes; repeat again and again these pure words: Gobind, Damodar, Madhav. ॥62॥
1359.10: (One who,) drunk with passion for woman, is proud, mighty, a doer of violence, and does not worship the lotus feet (of God), is the equal of a straw; cursed is his life. O ant, (if) the remembrance of Gobind is your wealth, (small as you are,) you are the weightiest. Nanak bows (to the Lord) countless times. ॥63॥
1359.11: The straw becomes Mount Meru, the withered turns green, the drowning swims across, the empty is filled, the light of millions of suns shines in the darkness: Nanak prays: (this is when) the Lord, the Guru, is merciful. ॥64॥
1360.1: In the company of the Brahmin who is perfect in the work of Brahm (God), one is saved; but those whose minds are steeped (in the world) and who cling to the world, O Nanak, those men are fruitless. ॥65॥
1360.2: (Those who) steal the wealth of others, raise many obstacles, and say all manner of things for their own livelihood, (who cry) let me take, let me take, in their craving, their minds never sated by Maya: they do the deeds of swine. ॥66॥
1360.3: Those who, rapt (in love), are absorbed in (God's) feet are delivered from the fearful (world) so hard to cross; countless sins are taken away, O Nanak, by the company of the Saadh: of this there is no doubt. ॥67॥

1353.1: There is one God, Ik Oankar, the One who pervades all and is ever the same; his Name is Sat (the One who truly is); he is the Creator, the Being who dwells in all, without fear, without enmity, his form beyond time, unborn, self-existent, realised by the Guru's grace.
Salok Sahaskriti, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
(The pandit) reads the books, says the sandhya prayers, and disputes;
he worships stone (idols), and sits in trance like a heron;
lies are on his lips, (decked out) like fine ornaments;
three times a day he ponders the three-footed (Gayatri);
a rosary round his neck, a tilak on his brow;
two dhotis, and a cloth over his head.
One who knows the work of (worshipping) God
(sees that) all these rites are surely hollow.
Says Nanak, one should meditate (on God) with firm faith,
(but) without the True Guru one does not find the way. ॥1॥
1353.2: Fruitless is the birth of that one, so long as he does not know Brahm (God).
By the Guru's grace many cross over the ocean of the world.
(God) is the Cause of creation, all-powerful: says Nanak, after reflection,
the cause (of all) is in the power of the Creator, who has established his power (in all creation). ॥2॥
1353.3: The way of the yogi is knowledge; the way of the Brahmins is the Veda;
the way of the Khatri is valour; the way of the Shudra is the service of others;
the way of all is (the remembrance of) the One; if anyone knows this secret,
Nanak is his servant; he himself is (the image of) Niranjan, the Lord. ॥3॥
1353.4: The one Krishna (the Lord) is the soul of all the gods, and the soul too of the gods of the gods;
(in all) is the soul of Sri Vasudev (the Lord); if anyone knows this secret,
Nanak is his servant; he himself is (the image of) Niranjan, the Lord. ॥4॥
1353.5: Salok Sahaskriti, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).

There is one God, Ik Oankar, the One who pervades all and is ever the same; his Name is Sat (the One who truly is); he is the Creator, the Being who dwells in all, without fear, without enmity, his form beyond time, unborn, self-existent, realised by the Guru's grace.
Where (in the end) are mother and father, where the joys of wife and sons?
Where are brother, friend, well-wisher and kin, and where the attachment to family?
Where is the fickle beauty of the enchantress (Maya)? Even before one's eyes she forsakes him.
Only the remembrance of the Lord stays with one; O Nanak, it is obtained from the sons of the Unshakeable One (the Sants). ॥1॥
1354.1: Cursed is attachment to mother and father; cursed is attachment to brothers and kin;
cursed is attachment to the delights of wife and sons;
cursed is attachment to the goods of the household.
Love for the Saadh Sangat (the company of the holy) alone is true and lasting; O Nanak, (those who keep it) dwell in peace. ॥2॥
1354.2: The body is perishable, its strength wanes;
old age advances, and with it love for Maya;
hopes grow beyond measure, (yet one is here) like a guest in the house;
fearsome Dharam Raj (the judge of souls) is counting (his) breaths.
The human body, so hard to obtain, falls into the well of attachment; O Nanak, his alone is the refuge:
the grace of Gobind (the Lord of the universe), Gobind, Gobind, Gopal (the Lord who sustains all), (alone saves). ॥3॥
1354.3: (The body) is a fort of unbaked clay, fashioned of water (seed), plastered with blood and skin;
it has nine doors, but no panels to them; it is propped up by the pillar of air (the breath).
The ignorant do not remember the Name of Gobind, and think (this body) will last forever.
O Nanak, in the refuge of the Saadh (the holy one), they save this body so hard to obtain,
who repeat Har Har Har Har Har Hare. ॥4॥
1354.4: You shine forth, O Unshakeable One, knower of virtues, all-pervading, abundant in mercy;
you are dear to your servants; your feet are (their) resting place.
O Master of the masterless, Nanak is in your refuge. ॥5॥
1354.5: Seeing a doe, the hunter takes aim and strikes with his weapons;
but behold, O Nanak: one whom Gopal protects has not a single hair pierced. ॥6॥
1354.6: One may strive in many ways and do mighty deeds, with warriors serving him on all four sides;
he may live in some lofty, hard-to-reach place and never call death to mind;
(yet) when the command of the Lord, the Primal Being, comes, O Nanak, an ant draws out (his) breath. ॥7॥
1354.7: Love for the Shabad, a heart set on kindness, the praise (of God): one who does these deeds in Kalyug,
the doubt and attachment lodged there (within him) are erased;
(to him) the Lord (is seen) pervading every place.
(O God,) your glance and your sight never fail to bear fruit; you dwell on the tongue of the Saadhs.
Says Nanak: O Lord, Har Har Har Hare, dear (to them) is the repeating of your Name. ॥8॥
1354.8: Beauty perishes, the continents perish, the sun, the moon, the stars and the sky perish;
the earth, the high-peaked mountains and the trees perish;
wife, sons, brothers and dear ones perish;
gold, gems and (all) the forms of Maya perish.
Only Gopal, the Unshakeable One, does not perish;
1354.9: No delay in doing right, delay in doing wrong;
fixing the Name firmly (in the heart), giving up greed;
destroying sins in the refuge of the Sants: these marks of dharma are gained
by the one, O Nanak, with whom Madhav (the Lord) is well pleased. ॥10॥
1354.10: One of shallow understanding stays absorbed in love of what perishes, in the play and the pleasures of a wife;
many-coloured mansions, fine clothes: thus does Maya hold sway over him.
O Unshakeable One, refuge of the Sants, O Lord, Nanak bows to you. ॥11॥
1354.11: Where there is birth, there is death; where joy, sorrow; where indulgence, disease;
where high, low; where small, great;
where rule, pride; where arrogance, humiliation.
On the path of worldly life, destruction holds sway.
The worship of Gobind in the company of the Saadh alone is lasting; O Nanak, the worship of the Lord is the food (of the soul). ॥12॥
1355.1: Where the Lord shows grace, the understanding gains the knowledge of what is real;
(such) wise ones blossom, (their understanding) becomes the home of happiness;
giving up pride, they keep their senses under control;
their hearts are cooled, and the wisdom of the Sants is fixed firm (within them).
absorbed in the sight of the Lord, they are freed from (further) birth;
O Nanak, the vina of the Shabad resounds (within them). ॥13॥
1355.2: The Vedas speak, the learned ponder, the students listen, in many ways and of many kinds;
(but those to whom) the Lord, Har Har, is merciful fix the highest learning (of the Name) firmly within.
O Nanak, they beg the gift of the Name from the Giver, Gopal, the Guru. ॥14॥
1355.3: No anxiety (is needed) for mother, father or brothers, no anxiety at all for other people;
no anxiety for wife, sons and friends, ties formed by involvement in Maya.
The one merciful Lord, the Primal Being, O Nanak, is the sustainer of all beings. ॥15॥
1355.4: Wealth does not last, thoughts (of it) do not last, hopes of many kinds do not last;
for love of what does not last, bound by ego, one wanders after Maya, (doing) foul and sinful deeds.
The one of soiled understanding, who does not remember (God), wanders through many births and the fire of the womb.
Says Nanak: O Gobind, show mercy, (grant) the company of the Saadh, the saviour of the fallen. ॥16॥
1355.5: Falling from a mountain into the nether world, burning in blazing fire,
being swept away on the waves of fathomless waters: against the pain of household cares, of birth and death,
many such practices do not succeed; O Nanak, the support, the support, the support is the Shabad of the Saadhs, the good. ॥17॥
1355.6: Terrible suffering, many killings, the poverty of births, great strife:
all are erased by remembering the Name of the Lord, O Nanak, as fire turns wood to ashes. ॥18॥
1355.7: Remembering (God), darkness turns to light; dwelling on (his) virtues, sins are destroyed;
when (he) dwells in the heart, Death's messengers are struck with fear, and one does deeds supremely pure;
the listener (to his praise) is freed from birth and death; his sight, never in vain, (brings) every comfort.
That Lord, mighty to give refuge, beloved of the Sants, O Nanak, brings well-being. ॥19॥
1355.8: (God) makes those left behind into leaders, and fulfils the hope of the hopeless;
(by his grace) the poor become rich; he cuts away the diseases of the sick;
to his devotees he gives the gift of devotion, of the Name of Ram and of the singing of his virtues.
The Supreme Lord, the Primal Being, is the Giver; O Nanak, what is not found through serving the Guru? ॥20॥
1355.9: The Name of Narhar is the support of the unsupported, the wealth of the poor;
Gobind is the master of the masterless, Keshav the strength of the weak;
the Unshakeable One is merciful to all beings, Damodar the kinsman of the lowly;
the all-knowing Lord, the Being who pervades all, loves devotion and is compassion itself;
Vasudev, the Supreme Lord, the Supreme God, dwells in every heart.
Nanak begs this grace of the Merciful One: may Narayan never be forgotten, never be forgotten. ॥21॥
1356.1: I have no strength, I am no servant, I have no love (for you), O Supreme Being, highest of beings;
by your grace alone, O merciful Lord, Har Har, the Guru, Nanak remembers (your) Name. ॥22॥
1356.2: (God) nourishes and sustains (all) beings, and gives the gifts of shelter and clothing;
the wise and conscious (Lord) creates the jewel of (human) birth.
By his grace (beings) live in comfort and bliss; those who remember the Lord, Har Har Hare, O Nanak, stay free of attachment to the passing creation. ॥23॥
1356.3: Through gifts given in former lives, kings enjoy (their realms);
but those whose understanding turns perverse in this mortal world, O Nanak, suffer pain for a long time. ॥24॥
1356.4: Those who are bereft of Gobind's grace, in whose hearts is no remembrance of him,
even when healthy are gravely ill, for they have forgotten the Compassionate One. ॥25॥
1356.5: To dwell only on the praise (of God) is the highest dharma of those who bear a body.
O Nanak, drinking the Amrit Name of Narayan, the Sants are never sated. ॥26॥
1356.6: The Sants are forbearing by nature; to them friend and evil-doer are alike;
O Nanak, (friends) come to them with food of many kinds, and slanderers come at them with weapons. ॥27॥
1356.7: They are never scorned, never dishonoured;
they are never without glory, and the sorrows of the world do not touch them,
who, joining the company of the Saadh, repeat the Name of Gobind; O Nanak, those mortals dwell in peace. ॥28॥
1356.8: The Saadhs together are an army of unconquerable warriors; humility is the armour on their bodies;
their weapons are the singing of Gobind's virtues; the shelter of the Guru's Shabad is the shield they hold;
knowing the way to God is the horses, chariots and elephants they ride;
they move without fear among the enemy's army, and charge (it) with the praise of Gopal;
they conquer the whole world, O Nanak, and bring the five thieves (lust, anger, greed, attachment and pride) under control. ॥29॥
1356.9: The one of evil understanding takes to heart a mirage (the deer's thirst), a city seen in the clouds (gandharv nagar), the shade of a tree;
just so false is attachment to family; O Nanak, (the Sants) remember the Name, Ram Ram. ॥30॥
1356.10: I am no treasury of the learning of the Vedas, no judge of virtues, nor have I the singing of the Name;
no jewel of melody is in my throat, nor am I quick, clever and shrewd;
Maya is gained by destiny and effort; (but) O Nanak, in the Saadh Sangat the fool (becomes) a pandit. ॥31॥
1356.11: One whose beautiful necklace is (the repeating of) Ram Ram, whose rosary-bag (hasat uch) is the love held (in the heart),
who utters with the tongue the sublime verses (of praise): he is saved from (Maya), the delight of the eyes. ॥32॥
1356.12: The mortal who is without the Guru's mantra: cursed is the life of that corrupt one;
that fool is the equal of a dog, a pig, a donkey, a crow, a snake. ॥33॥
1356.13: One who worships the lotus feet (of God) and holds the Name in the heart,
and sings the praise (of God) in the Saadh Sangat: O Nanak, Death's messengers do not even look at him. ॥34॥
1357.1: Wealth and beauty are not hard to obtain, nor is the kingdom of heaven hard to obtain;
fine foods and relishes are not hard to obtain, nor are clean clothes hard to obtain;
sons, friends, brothers and kin are not hard to obtain, nor are the pleasures of a wife hard to obtain;
skill in learning is not hard to obtain, nor is it hard to be clever and quick;
hard to obtain is the Name of the one Lord alone; O Nanak, it is found in the Saadh Sangat, by God's grace. ॥35॥
1357.2: Wherever one looks, there (God) is seen: in heaven, on earth, in the nether world;
Gobind pervades all places; O Nanak, no stain, no blemish touches (him). ॥36॥
1357.3: Poison becomes Amrit, enemies become friends and one's own people;
pain becomes comfort, and the one gripped by fear becomes fearless;
the homeless find a resting place in the Name, O Nanak, (when) the Lord, Har Har, the Guru, is merciful. ॥37॥
1357.4: The giver of a gentle nature to all gives it to me; the purifier of all is my purifier;
the maker of all is my maker; O Nanak, no stain, no blemish touches (him). ॥38॥
1357.5: The moon god is not (so) cooling, nor is the fragrant white sandal (bawan chandan);
nor is the winter season (so) cooling; O Nanak, it is the Saadhs, the good, who bring coolness. ॥39॥
1357.6: The Name, Ram Ram, for one's mantra; meditating on (God) as filling all places;
understanding pain and pleasure as alike; a way of life pure and free of enmity;
kindness to all beings everywhere; keeping clear of the five faults;
the praise of Gopal for one's food; remaining untouched by Maya, as the lotus in the water;
the teaching to hold friend and foe alike; loving devotion to the Lord;
not listening with the ears to the slander of others; giving up self-conceit and (becoming) the dust of all:
the perfect beings have these six marks; O Nanak, they are named the Saadhs, the good. ॥40॥
1357.7: A goat may feed on roots and tubers, but it lives near a lion:
such is the state of the world; O Nanak, sorrow and joy (alike) keep it in their grip. ॥41॥
1357.8: Deceit, faults, countless obstacles, offences, sins and filth,
doubt, attachment, honour and dishonour, and pride: (those over whom) Maya (thus) holds sway
wander through death and birth and hells; many remedies (tried) do not succeed.
Pure (become those who) in the company of the Saadh, O Nanak, repeat the Name of Gopal,
and dwell on the virtues of Gobind day after day. ॥42॥
1357.9: The refuge of the Master is a boat (to carry across); the Supreme God delights in play;
the Cause of creation, the all-powerful, the perfect God, gives gifts;
he fulfils the hope of the hopeless; he is the home of all good things.
O Nanak, all remember the treasure of virtues; all beg (of him) as beggars. ॥43॥
1357.10: Places hard to reach become easy; great sufferings all turn to comfort;
faithless slanderers who in their wandering pierced (others) with harsh words become good people;
sorrow settles into joy, and the one wasted by fears becomes fearless;
the fearful forest becomes a great city to dwell in: these marks of dharma (come) by God's grace:
dwelling on Ram Ram in the company of the Saadh, and refuge, O Nanak, at the feet of the merciful Lord, Har Har. ॥44॥
1358.1: O (attachment), you are the unconquered warrior of the battle, mighty beyond measure, the crusher of many;
ganas, gandharvas, gods, humans, beasts and birds: (all) you bewitch.
Nanak bows to the Lord, the Creator, (and takes) the refuge of the Lord of the world. ॥45॥
1358.2: O lust, you give a dwelling in hell, and make (beings) wander through many births;
you steal the mind, your reach is in all three worlds, you tear apart prayer, austerity and good conduct;
fickle one, you give little pleasure and leave (beings) bereft (of the wealth of virtue); you pervade the high and the low.
In the company of the Saadh one is freed from fear of you; Nanak (has taken) the shelter of Narayan. ॥46॥
1358.3: O anger, root of strife, compassion never springs up (in you);
you bring sensual beings under your sway, and make them dance like a monkey;
Death's messengers punish with many decrees the men made base in your company.
The merciful God, destroyer of the pains of the lowly, O Nanak, protects all beings. ॥47॥
1358.4: O greed, even the foremost are sunk in your company, and frolic on your countless waves;
beings (in your grip) run about in many ways, and waver in many fashions;
because of you, they have no shame before friend, nor revered one, nor kin, nor mother and father;
(in your power, one) openly does what should not be done, eats what should not be eaten, contrives what should not be contrived.
Nanak's prayer to the Lord, Narhar: save me, save me, O Master, (I am in your) refuge. ॥48॥
1358.5: O pride, root of birth and death, sinful of soul,
(under you) beings forsake friends and hold fast to enemies, spreading out Maya's many sprawls;
coming and going, beings grow weary, and suffer much pain and pleasure;
in doubt they wander in a fearsome wilderness, (caught in) dreadful, incurable diseases.
The physician is the Supreme Lord, the Supreme God; O Nanak, worship (him), Har Har Hare. ॥49॥
1358.6: O Gobind, Master of the breath of life, store of mercy, Guru of the world;
O remover of the world's fever, embodiment of compassion, take away all suffering;
O mighty to give refuge, home of mercy, Master of the meek, show grace,
(that) in the body's health and in its decline Nanak may remember (you), O Ram, Damodar, Madhav. ॥50॥
1358.7: The refuge of the lotus feet (of God), the uttering of Gopal's praise,
(through these,) in the company of the Saadh, O Nanak, one crosses the great ocean, so fearful and so hard to cross. ॥51॥
1358.8: The Supreme Lord guards the head and brow, the Supreme God guards the hands and body;
Gopal, the Master, guards the soul, the Lord of the world guards wealth and feet;
the merciful Guru (God) guards all, and destroys fear and pain.
Lover of devotion, Master of the masterless: Nanak (has come to) the refuge of the Unshakeable Being. ॥52॥
1358.9: He whose power holds up the sky, and keeps fire wrapped within wood;
whose power has set light in moon, sun and stars, and breath in bodies;
whose power sustains (beings) in the mother's womb, (so that) the affliction of the womb does not destroy them;
by that power he props up the lake (of the world); O Nanak, the waves of its water do not destroy (its beings). ॥53॥
1359.1: The Master of the world is supreme in being; remembering him is the life of all.
Through the company of the Sants, O Nanak, is found the pure path of devotion to the Lord. ॥54॥
1359.2: The mosquito shatters the mountain, the ant crosses the mire,
the cripple crosses the ocean, the darkness of the blind turns to light,
(when beings) remember Gobind through the company of the Saadh; Nanak (has come to) the refuge of the Lord, Har Har Hare. ॥55॥
1359.3: As a Brahmin without the tilak, as a king without command,
as a warrior without weapons: so, O Nanak, is a devotee (Vaishnav) without dharma. ॥56॥
1359.4: (God holds) no conch, no discus, no mace, nor is he dark of hue;
his form is wondrous, he is beyond birth;
the Vedas say (of him): neti neti (not this, not this);
The Unshakeable One dwells in the hearts of the Saadhs; O Nanak, the fortunate understand (this). ॥57॥
1359.5: One's dwelling is the wilderness of the world, where one's kin are dogs, jackals and donkeys;
the mind (is in) a perilous place, (drunk on) the wine of attachment, (beset by) the five thieves, mighty and untamed;
(there is) wandering in fondness, attachment, fear and doubt, and the noose of ego, sharp and hard;
the fire (of craving) and the water (of the senses) are untameable and dreadful; the shore is beyond reach and cannot be crossed to.
O Nanak, worship Gopal in the Saadh Sangat; in the refuge of the Lord's feet, by his grace, is deliverance. ॥58॥
1359.6: When Gobind, Gopal, shows mercy, he cuts away all diseases;
in the company of the Saadh, O Nanak, one dwells on (his) virtues, (abiding) in the refuge of the perfect Supreme God. ॥59॥
1359.7: A man may be handsome and sweet of speech, but in the soil of his heart is enmity;
(then his) bowing is false; the Sants, the good, stay alert (to it). ॥60॥
1359.8: The heedless fool does not know that (his) breaths grow fewer day by day;
the most beautiful body wastes away, devoured by the daughter of Death (old age);
the man stays absorbed in the play of family, in hopes of Maya's passing pleasures;
wandering and wandering through many births, (the soul) is worn out; Nanak (has come to) the refuge of the Compassionate One. ॥61॥
1359.9: O tongue, O lover of tastes, sweet things are dear to you;
to the True (Name) you are dead, (and you raise) great disputes; repeat again and again these pure words:
1359.10: (One who,) drunk with passion for woman, is proud,
and does not worship the lotus feet (of God), is the equal of a straw; cursed is his life.
O ant, (if) the remembrance of Gobind is your wealth, (small as you are,) you are the weightiest.
Nanak bows (to the Lord) countless times. ॥63॥
1359.11: The straw becomes Mount Meru, the withered turns green,
the drowning swims across, the empty is filled,
the light of millions of suns shines in the darkness:
Nanak prays: (this is when) the Lord, the Guru, is merciful. ॥64॥
1360.1: In the company of the Brahmin who is perfect in the work of Brahm (God), one is saved;
but those whose minds are steeped (in the world) and who cling to the world, O Nanak, those men are fruitless. ॥65॥
1360.2: (Those who) steal the wealth of others, raise many obstacles, and say all manner of things for their own livelihood,
(who cry) let me take, let me take, in their craving, their minds never sated by Maya: they do the deeds of swine. ॥66॥
1360.3: Those who, rapt (in love), are absorbed in (God's) feet are delivered from the fearful (world) so hard to cross;
countless sins are taken away, O Nanak, by the company of the Saadh: of this there is no doubt. ॥67॥
